transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Samir (AtlasFin Head ML), Marta (AtlasFin Head Data), Dana (Infra), Owen (Security), Kelly (Product)

Summary (auto): Discussed options for keeping vector data on-prem due to regulatory constraints while using Redwood for reranking and model serving. Explored tradeoffs in embedding size, throughput, and where rerank should live.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, we'll kick off with a little context from AtlasFin then Priya and Marco will run through how Redwood can slot into that flow, ok?
[00:12] Samir (AtlasFin): Yeah thanks. I run ML at AtlasFin, we build credit decisioning features, so PII concerns are real. main ask: we need vectors not to leave our VPC, but we'd like to use a hosted or dedicated rerank model that Redwood manages. curious how that can work and what the latency/cost will look like.
[00:30] Marta (AtlasFin): and we want to support both nearline historical search and low-latency fanout for current session lookups. throughput: roughly 1k qps at peak across microservices, avg 200 qps.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): great context. couple quick clarifying q's: when you say keep vectors on-prem, do you mean on your managed Milvus clusters in the VPC, or on bare-metal in an air-gapped facility?
[00:55] Dana (AtlasFin): it's managed Milvus in our VPC for now. we may have an air-gapped site in a year but pilot is VPC-bound.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood SE): ok perfect. so two high-level patterns we usually see: 1) vectors stored and searched in your VPC (Milvus/Pinecone) and we call into it, with Redwood doing the rerank either hosted or via a dedicated capacity inside your VPC; or 2) hybrid: lightweight recall in VPC and candidate rerank in Redwood hosted, with encrypted payloads and strict logging. each has pros/cons.
[01:25] Marco (Redwood SE): latency wise if rerank is hosted off-VPC you add network RTT plus model latency, so for tail latency sensitive flows we usually recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment (private control plane + on-prem or VPC data plane).
[01:40] Owen (AtlasFin - Security): we need KMS integration, HSM for key custody ideally, and audit logs for every inference that touches PII. SOC2 is baseline. also SSO for console and RBAC. can Redwood do HSM-backed keys?
[01:55] Alex (Redwood): yes, we support external KMS providers for Private and Dedicated; HSM-backed keys can be integrated for Private deployments. we also surface audit logs and can stream them to your SIEM. we'll include SOC2 docs in the drop.
[02:10] Kelly (AtlasFin - Product): how invasive is the private control plane? we're wary of heavy ops overhead.
[02:18] Priya (Redwood SE): private control plane is minimal — Redwood orchestrates, but the data plane lives in your VPC. for the pilot you can choose a managed Dedicated tenant in the same cloud region which is faster to stand up; Private is more work but required for higher regulatory needs.
[02:32] Samir (AtlasFin): ok, makes sense. curious on some of the embedding decisions — we're currently using 1536 dims for our in-house model and it gives better retrieval quality, but cost is mounting. any suggestions?
[02:45] Marco (Redwood SE): common tradeoff: 1536 gives more representational power but doubles storage and increases nearest-neighbor compute. sometimes teams quantize to 8-bit or use 768 dim student models for fanout and then rerank with 1536 on the top-K. Redwood supports per-route model variants and automatic fallback to higher-dim rerank models.
[03:05] Marta (AtlasFin): the hybrid student-student+teacher idea sounds promising. what's the overhead of moving from 768->1536 in your benchmarks?
[03:15] Priya (Redwood SE): it depends on hardware and vector DB. roughly storage ~2x, search CPU/GPU ops up by 1.8x in our tests. but if you do recall with 768 and rerank top 50 with 1536 locally, the end-to-end latency can stay acceptable and cost reduces significantly.
[03:32] Samir: what's the fastest path to get a pilot? we want to validate accuracy/latency with our live queries.
[03:38] Alex: we usually run a 2-week pilot: Redwood Dedicated with a small reserved pool colocated in your cloud region, run throughput benchmarks (with your sample queries), and compare recall + rerank accuracy vs current baseline. for PII constraints we can also do Private if your security team wants HSM and no outbound data.
[03:55] Dana: for the pilot we can give you 1k qps replay for 30 minutes and a golden set of labeled matches. throughput question: Redwood's dedicated will autoscale?
[04:06] Marco: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity, yes. for consistent 1k qps we'll recommend a small reserved pool and a burstable config. Priya: we should sketch sizing.
[04:18] Priya: quick sizing note: if you do 768 dims for recall and 1536 for rerank within Redwood, plan for network serialization cost on candidate payloads. targeting 200-400ms p95 for rerank hosted is realistic with dedicated GPUs; private/VPC local rerank can get to sub-100ms p95 depending on colocation.
[04:39] Owen: sub-100ms is important for interactive flows. where do you usually run the KV cache and prefix caching? inside Redwood?
[04:46] Priya: we offer automatic prefix and KV cache in the data plane. if data plane is in your VPC those caches are local, reducing RTT. otherwise our hosted cache sits in Redwood's infra and adds a hop.
[04:58] Kelly: curious about vector DB integrations — we run Milvus and some older clusters on ElasticSearch/OpenSearch. how smooth is the integration?
[05:06] Marco: we have connectors and have integrated with Milvus and Pinecone commonly. for OpenSearch it's more custom but doable. common pattern: run ANN recall with Milvus and return top-N ids; Redwood fetches payloads and does rerank. we can also run embedding generation in-host or let you precompute and bring vectors.
[05:23] Samir: we'd prefer to precompute and keep embeddings internal. is there any place that requires sending the raw vector to Redwood?
[05:30] Priya: not required. you can host vectors and send only IDs + payloads for rerank. if you prefer Redwood to compute rerank embeddings with a model, we can accept encrypted vectors too but for compliance best is to keep embeddings in the VPC and only send opaque candidate ids and metadata for scoring.
[05:48] Dana: what about model updates and versioning? we can't have silent degradations.
[05:52] Alex: Redwood supports pinned model versions per-route and rollout controls (canary, A/B). we also tie regressions to prompt sets/evals and can alert on quality drifts. we'll include an eval harness in the pilot to track regression.
[06:05] Marta: on the eval side we want to be able to re-run rerank models locally. do you provide model binaries or only hosted endpoints for rerank?
[06:13] Marco: for Private we can provide a package that runs in your environment; Dedicated is managed but can be isolated to your tenant; hosted endpoints are fully managed. Private gives you the most control for reproducibility.
[06:25] Samir: cost — high level. if we do 1k peak qps with recall in Milvus and rerank top 50 in Redwood dedicated, what's ballpark cost?
[06:33] Alex: rough guesstimate depends on model size and token counts, but ballpark per-month for a small dedicated pool sized for that throughput is in the mid-five-figure range. we'll provide a sizing + pricing sheet.
[06:44] Kelly: any gotchas with logging and PII? we need redaction and token-level audit.
[06:50] Owen: yes and SIEM forwarding.
[06:53] Priya: we support configurable data retention, token-level breakdowns, and streaming audit logs to your SIEM for Private/Dedicated. hosted API has standard retention but for regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[07:05] Samir: ok this is helpful. one more deep question: can you do on-the-fly quantized rerank to reduce memory without losing too much accuracy?
[07:14] Marco: yes, model quantization and compilers in our runtime can run INT8/4-bit modes; for rerank models we often quantize to 8-bit and validate accuracy. sometimes a small accuracy delta is acceptable if latency and cost wins are large. we'll run the quantized eval for your golden set in the pilot.
[07:32] Marta: timeline we are targeting: internal POC in July, decision by end of July to kick off pilot early August.
[07:40] Alex: sounds good. next steps recap in a minute.
[07:45] Kelly: before we wrap — do you have references in fintech?
[07:49] Alex: yes, we can share anonymized case studies; lunch-and-learn intros possible.
[07:55] Priya: quick recap of technical asks from this call: sample queries + labeled set, clear latency SLO targets, clarifying the split (recall in VPC vs rerank managed), list of required compliance controls. we'll also produce a benchmark plan and recommended dedicated sizing.
[08:12] Samir: perfect. thanks.

Auto-generated action items (end): Alex to send pricing and architecture, Priya to send benchmark plan, AtlasFin to send samples and security checklist.

End of meeting.
